title: Can Deregulation Drive Services Spending?
text:
Can Deregulation Drive Services Spending?

Ernan Cui

Gavekal Dragonomics | 14 Aug 2026

After two years of high-level policies that subsidized consumer purchases of goods, China’s policymakers are shifting their focus to services. The government is still looking for ways to support domestic demand, but households’ near-term demand for autos, appliances and other subsidized goods has now been exhausted. The government is thus pursuing new avenues, and the structural rise in services consumption makes them a more promising target. A flurry of recent government documents have pledged to lift services spending, and the Politburo’s midyear meeting on the economy called on officials to “tap the potential of services consumption.”
